Overview:
## Circuit Element Defaults
In WindMil and DisSPatch: 

Go to Preferences|Circuit Element Defaults... to open the Circuit Element Defaults dialog. 

In WindMilMap: 

Go to WindMilMap|Circuit Element Defaults... to open the Circuit Element Defaults dialog. 

The Circuit Element Preferences dialog sets the defaults used when creating various types of circuit elements. These defaults should be set to the most commonly used settings. 

The Circuit Element Defaults dialog 

When a new circuit element is created or added to the system where a valid system preference is defined, it will be used to initialize that field. The exception to this is that overhead and underground circuit elements will first look for the first upline element of the same type. If a like type ancestor is found, Conductor Type and Construction Type will be inherited from that upline element.
generator:
## Generator Model 
A drop-down box that contains the following options: 

### Negative Load 
A model that assumes that the generator’s kW and kvar output to be fixed load negative to non-generator loads. This model is useful when the generator’s output is small compared to the capacity of the circuit. In the negative load model, the generator has no ability to hold a specified voltage. 

### Swing kvar 
A model that assumes that the generator is a source of fixed kW to the circuit and a variable source of kvar as required to hold a specified voltage magnitude at the generator. 

## Total Generator kVA 
The desired total kW and kvar output for the generator. If kvar is set, then PF is calculated. If PF is set, then kvar is calculated. 

The specified kW will be modeled as a negative load or as a source of kW to the circuit. The kvar will be modeled negative to its specified sign. A positive PF will be seen as a source of kvar to the circuit, and a negative PF will be seen as a kvar load to the circuit. (Tip: Only available if the generator model is set to Negative Load.)

## Generator is to hold 
The magnitude of voltage (per unit) that the generator is to maintain. (Tip: Only available if the generator model is set to Swing kvar.)

## Output is set at 
The kW output of the generator. This will be the fixed kW injected into the circuit by the generator. (Tip: Only available if the generator model is set to Swing kvar.)

## Maximum leading output is 
Specifies the maximum leading (positive) kvar output of the generator. The algorithm will not limit the kvar at this level, but will flag the generator graphically (and on printouts) if it exceeds this limit. (Tip: Only available if the generator model is set to Swing kvar.)

## Maximum lagging output is 
Specifies the maximum lagging (negative) kvar output of the generator. The algorithm will not limit the kvar at the given level, but will flag the generator graphically (and on printouts), if it exceeds this limit. (Tip: Only available if the generator model is set to Swing kvar.)
switch:
Switches have two sides. When you create a switch object, WindMil creates both sides of the switch. To one of these sides, WindMil appends -A to signify that side is the A partner of the switch. To the other, it appends -B. 

The following options control whether the Circuit Element Editor will let you change a switch partner's name so that the name does not contain -A or -B. 

## Automatically rename partner and append –A or –B 
Renames the switch partner with up to 18 characters. WindMil adds the –A or –B to the name. The actual total number of characters allowed is 20, which includes the –A or –B. 

## Manually set partner without appending –A or –B 
Renames the switch partner with up to 20 characters. You must manually rename the switch’s partner by using the Navigator or Circuit Element Editor. The name must be unique because WindMil will not append the –A or –B.
node:
## Node is Mandatory 
Determines whether new nodes will be mandatory nodes. Mandatory nodes are used by Circuit Reducer to flag sections that should not be eliminated during the reduction process. 

## Circuit Level 
Defines what sort of item this node will represent.
conductor:
## All Phases the Same 
Specifies whether new lines are expected to have the same equipment on all phases. 

## Phase Conductor 
The default conductor equipment for the existing phases of a new line. 

## Construction Code 
The default construction type for the new overhead or underground conductor. 

## Secondary Construction Code 
The default secondary construction type for the new overhead or underground conductor.
capacitor:
## All Phases the Same 
Specifies whether or not new capacitors will be set so that all phases are assumed to have the same kvar rating. 

## kV Rating 
The kV rating applied to a new capacitor. The recommended setting is “0.000”. 

## Status 
The default status for new capacitors. The recommended setting is On. 

## Switch Type 
The default switch type for a new capacitor. The recommended setting is Manual. 

## kvar/Phase 
The per phase kvar, which should be set to the most common system capacitor bank size.
source:
## Bus Voltage 
The per unit value of the bus voltage for new sources. 

## OH Ground 
The default value for the overhead ground ohms. 

## UG Ground 
The default value for the underground ground ohms. 

## Nominal L-G 
The default nominal line-to-ground value. Filling in this value will default the nominal line-to-line value by multiplying the line-to-ground by the square root of 3. 

## Nominal L-L 
The default nominal line-to-line value. Filling in this value will default the nominal line-to-ground by dividing the line-to-line by the square root of 3. 

## Source Connect 
The source connection type. The choices are Wye or Delta. 

## Regulation 
Specifies whether the new sources are Regulated or Unregulated.
transformer:
## Winding Connections 
Specifies the default winding connection for new transformers. 

## Transformer Imp Definition 
Contains the default transformer equipment for new transformers. 

## Default rated input voltage to base kV of parent element 
Automatically sets the rated input voltage of any newly-added transformer to the base voltage of their parent element. This only happens when the transformer is added. If the transformer is re-parented to another element with a different base voltage, the program will not automatically update the input voltage to match the new parent. 

If this box is left unchecked, the program will default the rated input voltage of new transformers to whatever values are given in the “Transformer” tab. 

## Center Tap first available phase 
Automatically sets the center tap phase of newly-added transformers to the element's first existing phase. For instance, the center tap phase of a BC transformer would be set to B, not C. Tip: This will only happen to transformers with a valid winding code (Y-D Grd, Y-D unGrd, Y-D one, Y-D open, D-D, D-D one, or D-D open).

## Primary Rated Input L-G 
The transformer's rated input line-to-ground value. Entering a value will default the line-to-line value, which is calculated by multiplying the line-to-ground value by the square root of 3. 

## Primary Rated Input L-L 
The transformer's rated input line-to-line value. Entering a value will default the line-to-ground value, which is calculated by dividing the line-to-line value by the square root of 3. 

## Primary Tap L-G 
The transformer's rated input line-to-ground value. Entering a value will default the line-to-line value, which is calculated by multiplying the line-to-ground value by the square root of 3. 

## Primary Tap L-L 
The transformer's rated input line-to-line value. Entering a value will default the line-to-ground value, which is calculated by dividing the line-to-line value by the square root of 3. 

## Rated Output L-G 
The transformer's output line-to-ground value. Entering a value will change the default line-to-line value, which is calculated by multiplying the line-to-ground value by the square root of 3. 

## Rated Output L-L 
The transformer's output line-to-line value. Entering a value will change the default line-to-ground value, which is calculated by dividing the line-to-line value by the square root of 3. 

## Nominal of Output L-G 
The default nominal line-to-ground value. Entering a value will change the default nominal line-to-line value, which is calculated by multiplying the line-to-ground value by the square root of 3. 

## Nominal of Output L-L 
The nominal line-to-line value. Entering a value will change the default nominal line-to-ground value, which is calculated by dividing the line-to-line value by the square root of 3.
regulator:
## All Phases the Same 
Specifies whether regulators will be created as having 1-Phase units with all phases the same or 1-Phase units with different settings. 

## Regulator Type 
Specifies whether the new regulators are single- or three-phase regulators. 

## Controlling Phase if 3-Phase 
Specifies which phase is the controlling phase if the regulator is three-phase. 

## Winding Connections 
Determines the default winding connection for the regulator. 

## Regulator Size Definition 
Contains information on the default regulator equipment for new regulators. 

## Output Voltage 
The default output voltage for new regulators. This number is a per unit value. 

## First House High 
The regulator's first house high default value. This number is a per unit value. 

## First House Low 
The regulator's first house low default value. This number is a per unit value.
OCD:
## All Phases the Same 
Specifies whether new devices are expected to have the same equipment on all phases. 

## Equipment 
The default equipment for the existing phases on a new device. 

## Open or Closed 
Specifies whether new devices are created open or closed.
motor:
## Total Motor hp 
The default motor size in horse power. 

## PF at Full Load 
The default motor full load and speed power factor. 

## Eff. at Full Load 
The default motor full load and speed efficiency rating. 

## Rated LG 
The default motor line-to-ground voltage. 

## Rated LL 
The default motor line-to-line voltage. 

## PF at Locked Rotor 
The default locked rotor power factor. 

## Nema Type Code 
The default motor Nema Type code. 

## Motor will not start if % is less than 
Defines the default motor pull out voltage. 

## Motor will drop out if % voltage is less than 
Defines the default motor drop out voltage.
consumer:
## Active consumer 
Specifies whether new consumers should be created as active or inactive. 

## Consumer Type 
The type of consumer element you wish to model. Because most utilities have many more residential consumers than other consumers, we recommend you set the default to Residential.
map_point:
## Newly created map points default to 
Specifies what kind of map point is added to the model by default.

## Edit Map Point Types 
Opens the Map Point Symbol Editor.
